low.description: Take a quiet moment to notice what’s going on inside you. There’s no need to fix anything—just observe what thoughts or feelings are present.

medium.description: Pause and gently name what you’re feeling—confused, heavy, restless, or unsure. Naming emotions can bring a little clarity.

high.description: When emotions feel intense, bring attention to your breath or body first. Feeling steady helps reflection feel safer.

low.description: Slow, steady breathing can help calm the body when anxiety feels mild or just beginning.

medium.description: Use your senses to gently anchor yourself in the present moment when anxious thoughts start looping.

high.description: When anxiety feels overwhelming, focus on calming the body first and seek support if needed.

low.description: Notice small moments where you could rest or pause, even briefly, during the day.

medium.description: When everything feels too much, focusing on one small step at a time can reduce pressure.

high.description: Feeling exhausted doesn’t mean you’ve failed. Acknowledging burnout and seeking rest or support can help.

low.description: Notice shifts in your mood without judging them. Awareness can prevent automatic reactions.

medium.description: Take a few slow breaths, name what you’re feeling, and choose how to respond instead of reacting quickly.

high.description: Strong emotional swings can feel destabilizing. Grounding and external support can help.

low.description: Feeling lonely doesn’t mean there’s something wrong with you. Acknowledging it can soften its intensity.

medium.description: Gently remind yourself that loneliness doesn’t define your worth or value.

high.description: When loneliness feels heavy, reaching out to someone you trust can help.

low.description: Feeling numb is a common response to emotional overload. Simply noticing it is enough for now.

medium.description: Try focusing on physical sensations—your feet on the floor or your breath—to reconnect with the present moment.

high.description: Persistent numbness can be a sign you need support. Grounding and human connection can help.

low.description: When things feel unclear, pause and focus on just this moment rather than the whole situation.

medium.description: Choose one small thing to focus on right now. Clarity often comes step by step.

high.description: When confusion feels overwhelming, slowing down and seeking support can help.

low.description: Reflect on what the conflict stirred up emotionally, without blaming yourself or others.

medium.description: Identify the feeling beneath the conflict—hurt, fear, or frustration—before responding.

high.description: Strong emotions after conflict are normal. Grounding and support can help settle things.

low.description: Academic pressure is common and doesn’t define your intelligence or worth.

medium.description: Breaking work into smaller priorities can reduce overwhelm.

high.description: When academic stress feels unmanageable, grounding and guidance can help.

low.description: Notice which parts of work feel draining versus manageable, without self-judgment.

medium.description: Consider where your energy is being stretched and where small boundaries could help.

high.description: Ongoing work stress benefits from rest and external support.

low.description: Money stress is heavy and common. It doesn’t reflect personal failure.

medium.description: Gently separate what you can control right now from what you can’t.

high.description: Severe financial stress can feel overwhelming. Grounding and support can help.

low.description: Create space for the user to share more, without introducing exercises yet.

medium.description: Notice thoughts as they come and go, without treating them as facts.

high.description: Focus on emotional safety and calming first.

low.description: Greet the user warmly and invite them to share how they are feeling today.

medium.description: Gently invite the user to share what’s been on their mind.

high.description: Respond with calm reassurance and emotional availability.

medium.description: I’m really sorry you’re going through this. You don’t have to face it alone. Reaching out to someone you trust can help.

high.description: I’m really sorry you’re feeling this much pain. Your safety matters most right now. Please contact a crisis helpline or emergency service immediately.
